author: reek
body: TrueType from the stick -- H4c. The guios font loader carries its own FAT32 walk over the block-read-sector syscall, which is dead on the Option A path (the stub never installs the syscall machinery firmware-side of runtime-init, and the boot medium may not even be an IDE disk). But everything after the sector reads is buffer-pure: fb-parse-ttf takes a flat byte buffer, fb-render-ascii rasterizes from it, fl-raster-to-gobf packs the coverage tables. So the port is one seam: read the TTF off the ESP with gfat-read-file-bulk -- the same driver stack that already reads the seed, riding the medium lock -- and hand the buffer to the unchanged guios pipeline.

author: reek
body: The rasterized font is a GopBitmapFont: 95 glyphs of 8-bit alpha coverage plus advance and y-offset tables, drawn by gbf-put-text with per-pixel blending against whatever is already on the panel.

author: reek
body: gbf-put-text wants a GopBuf; ours aliases the real framebuffer with the panel's stride standing as the buffer width, which is the only width gbf's pixel math uses.

author: val
body: UIFONT.CFG holds an ASCII FAT filename in a 16-byte, zero-padded record. Bulk FAT reads transfer whole sectors, so the configuration read reserves 1024 bytes even though the logical file is at most 16 bytes.

author: val
body: `gf-gh` is the CELL height and not the ppem, and the two differ. A face's bounding box may exceed its em, so cmunss at a 32 pixel em rasterizes into 41 rows (`FontLoad`, `fb-render-glyph`). Handing `ppem` to `fl-raster-to-gobf` therefore stored 32 of those 41 rows and cut the descenders off at the bottom of the box; the height comes off the rasters now, which is what `fl-max-height` was written for and was never called for. A caller wanting the type size still passes `ppem` in; a caller placing a line reads `gf-gh`.

author: val
body: The face is PROPORTIONAL: `fl-raster-to-gobf` writes a 95-entry advance table after the glyph bitmaps, and `gbf-put-text-loop` steps by it. So a string's width is not its length times anything, and a caller that bounds text by an assumed cell width will be wrong in both directions -- it truncates a narrow string early and lets a wide one overflow its box.
